collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and an elder)

collection.description: An elder tells a villager to sleep on a decision, but morning brings no answer: sleep on it again, or decide at breakfast.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has to decide whether to take on an apprentice. (friend) says, "Sleep on it. Things are clearer in the morning." So (subject) sleeps on it. In the morning, (subject.he/she) wakes up, lies in bed and checks. Nothing is clearer. If anything, it's foggier.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) decides to sleep on it another night. And another. By the fourth morning (subject.he/she) still doesn't know, but (subject.he/she) has slept very well. (friend) asks how it's going. "I'm well rested," says (subject). "And undecided." (friend) nods sagely. "That's allowed too." The apprentice question waits a while. Nobody minds.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: At breakfast, halfway through a mango, (subject) suddenly says "Yes" out loud. Everyone looks at (subject.him/her). "I'll take the apprentice," (subject.he/she) says. "I just decided." Maybe it was the sleeping. Maybe it was the mango. (friend) takes credit anyway, and (subject) lets (friend.him/her).
